title: Scoped negative result: 72/77 copy-cost lower bounds for two masked Walsh P112 totals
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Two masked Walsh source totals can leave the P112 coordinate column space, but this specific two-coordinate-reader family still cannot improve the copy-rank bill. A written support-cell reduction and exact finite premises give cost **at least 72 for every real coefficient matrix with two nonzero columns**, and **at least 77 when both masked sources are nonzero**, against the coordinate baseline 64. These continuous lower bounds are not asserted to be attained.

The separate exhaustive census covers all 28 coordinate pairs, 511 nonzero binary label cuts and 40 small unimodular matrices: **572,320 cases**, minimum 72 overall and 78 with both sources nonzero. The all-real argument reduces residual supports to six scalar representatives and added-reader supports to five types, then sums independent term minima as an optimistic lower bound. This is not an inference from a failed search.

Only `research/p112-masked-walsh/` is added. It contains the proof, source pins, deterministic certificate, geometry, two independent rank implementations, controls and local sprint claim. Exact base: `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`; OS assignment seed **48**, structural decoder research. No coordination issue existed at the original claim. The final October 14 refresh read the new coordination/handoff discussions and checked relevant P112 PRs through #1656. Main was `5e554ff58d01921747d27177045c0061f31e1ad1`, selected #1094 at kappa 0.001672660197076918; the consumed source heads stayed unchanged.

Credit **Mihir Srivastava's #845** at `125ce25bdae421627b56077adc14940c2d0aa52f` for the retained exact geometry and single-lift predecessor; **DreamingOfClouds' #717** at `4a97676294f9fa413b65986e9984fddeda71e4cc` for the model/open problem and #446 for the inherited copy interpretation; **Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled's #620** for the baseline 64. Source files and their notice are preserved verbatim. #1133's rational single-lift descent is distinct.

Concurrent overlap: **Philipp / @mightyOil's #1197** excludes, among other cases, disjoint added-reader coefficient supports. Here both readers can use the same `{p,q}`; disjoint source row supports are a different condition. This gives quantitative evidence for a specific subfamily of its overlapping-reader opening. **@thakrarsagar's #1327** studies a different two-sided parity lift, whose strengthened floor requires both factors off the root code; all our reader columns stay in col(X). #1191 concerns masked exactness, while our identity already holds on all pairs. #1375/#1460/#1473 use free-rectangle factorizations. Exact heads, additional adjacent work and scope comparisons are in `OVERLAP.json` and the README. The contribution is the specialized **72/77 certificate and independent census**, not a general decoder impossibility or priority claim.

Even granting preparation, source access, helpers, frame changes, restoration and recursive children zero extra cost, the copy bill loses. This does not exclude arbitrary two-total sources, dense reader changes, other masks, interacting delivery programs or improvements to other expenses. No physical supplier, new kappa, full multiplication proof or human peer review is claimed. Inherited compiler, hosting, precision/tape and analytic assumptions remain.

## Validation

Python 3.10+; standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/p112-masked-walsh/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/p112-masked-walsh/independent_check.py
python3 -I -B research/p112-masked-walsh/test_verify.py
```

Expected markers: `PASS_P112_MASKED_WALSH cases=572320 minimum=72 baseline=64 no_new_kappa`, `PASS_P112_MASKED_WALSH_INDEPENDENT`, and a passing unittest.

CPython 3.12.13 on macOS: all checks pass. The independent direct-pairing implementation matches every histogram and all 14,308 relaxation cases and checks 28 full endpoint identities. Isolated optimized relocation, source/geometry/receipt corruption rejection, missing-relaxation and duplicate-pair rejection, export preservation and staged whitespace pass. Uploaded file contents match the locally verified commit byte-for-byte. Repository-wide `make verify`, selected supplier cold replay, hosted CI and Lean were not run for this isolated package. The selected frontier and `upstream/` are unchanged.

Prepared for **Denis (@just-mn)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, mathematics, implementation, independent AI replay and writing. Apache-2.0; full attribution and limitations are in the package.
